pharm: Tetracycline antibiotic that reversibly binds the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, blocking aminoacyl-tRNA binding and inhibiting protein synthesis
quick: 250-500 mg orally every 6 hours (1-2 g/day) per indication
Take 1 h before or 2 h after food; avoid dairy/antacids/iron
Avoid - tetracyclines cause fetal tooth discoloration and affect bone growth
Generally avoid - excreted in milk (tooth/bone effects)
Avoid/caution in renal impairment - tetracyclines are anti-anabolic and accumulate
Caution - hepatotoxicity reported, especially with high IV doses
Best avoided; not a specific contraindication
Renal and hepatic function on prolonged therapy; signs of superinfection
summary: Oxytetracycline is a broad-spectrum bacteriostatic tetracycline antibiotic that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the 30S ribosome. It is used for susceptible infections including rickettsial diseases, atypical respiratory pathogens (Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila/psittacosis), chlamydial genital infections, acne and other tetracycline-susceptible organisms. Like all tetracyclines, it should be avoided during the second half of pregnancy, in lactation and in children under 8 years because it causes permanent tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia and may affect bone growth. Absorption is impaired by dairy, antacids and iron (cation chelation); photosensitivity, GI upset, esophageal ulceration (if taken at bedtime with little water) and (rarely) hepatotoxicity and C. difficile colitis can occur.
indications: Rickettsial infections (Rocky Mountain spotted fever, typhus group, Q fever, tick fevers)
Respiratory infections caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae
Chlamydial infections: psittacosis (Chlamydophila psittaci), trachoma and inclusion conjunctivitis, lymphogranuloma venereum, uncomplicated urogenital/rectal C. trachomatis infection
Other infections caused by susceptible Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms when a tetracycline is appropriate

dosage.d: 250-500 mg every 6 hours (usual 1-2 g/day in divided doses)
dosage.n: Continue at least 24-48 h after symptoms/fever resolve

dosage.d: Typically 250-500 mg twice daily, reducing once controlled

dosage.c: Uncomplicated genital chlamydial infection (where tetracycline used)
dosage.d: 500 mg four times daily for 7 days (per tetracycline-class regimens)

dosage.n: Do NOT use under 8 years (tooth staining)

admin: Take on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after food) with a full glass of water
Avoid dairy products, antacids, calcium/magnesium/aluminium and iron preparations near dosing (they chelate and reduce absorption)
Take with plenty of fluid and not immediately before lying down to avoid esophageal irritation/ulceration
Avoid in children under 8 years and in pregnancy/lactation (dental and bone effects)
moa: Oxytetracycline reversibly binds the 30S bacterial ribosomal subunit, preventing aminoacyl-tRNA from attaching to the mRNA-ribosome complex and thereby inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis. The effect is primarily bacteriostatic across a broad range of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, mycoplasmas, chlamydiae and rickettsiae.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to oxytetracycline or any tetracycline
Children under 8 years of age (except severe/life-threatening conditions with no alternative)
Pregnancy (second/third trimester) and breastfeeding - dental/bone effects
monitor: Renal and hepatic function on prolonged therapy

preg: Tetracyclines, including oxytetracycline, cross the placenta and can cause permanent discoloration of deciduous teeth and affect fetal bone growth when used in the second half of pregnancy. Avoid in pregnancy unless no safer alternative exists for a serious infection.
lact: Tetracyclines are excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for tooth discoloration and effects on bone in the infant, breastfeeding is generally not recommended during oxytetracycline therapy.
renal: Tetracyclines (other than doxycycline) are anti-anabolic and can accumulate in renal impairment, worsening azotemia, acidosis and hyperphosphataemia; avoid or use with caution and dose reduction in renal impairment.
hepatic: Hepatotoxicity, including fatty liver, has been reported (particularly with high parenteral doses or in pregnancy/renal impairment). Use with caution and monitor liver function.

major: Oral retinoids (isotretinoin/acitretin) - additive risk of benign intracranial hypertension; avoid combination
Methoxyflurane anesthesia - reports of fatal renal toxicity with tetracyclines
moderate: Antacids/iron/calcium/magnesium/aluminium and dairy - chelation markedly reduces absorption; separate dosing
Warfarin / oral anticoagulants - tetracyclines depress prothrombin activity; may need anticoagulant dose reduction
Penicillins / bactericidal antibiotics - bacteriostatic tetracyclines may antagonize their action
Combined oral contraceptives - may be rendered less effective (advise additional precautions)
minor: Barbiturates, carbamazepine, phenytoin - reduce tetracycline half-life (enzyme induction)
interactions.food: Take on an empty stomach; dairy and food (especially calcium-rich) reduce absorption
interactions.diagnostics: May depress plasma prothrombin activity (affecting INR); may cause false elevations on some urinary catecholamine assays

serious: Severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, erythema multiforme)
rare: Permanent tooth discoloration / enamel hypoplasia (in children/fetus)
emergency: Severe or bloody diarrhea (C. difficile colitis)
Severe headache with visual disturbance (intracranial hypertension)

monitoring: Renal and hepatic function during prolonged or high-dose therapy
Symptoms of raised intracranial pressure (headache, blurred vision) in at-risk patients
counsel: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water, 1 hour before or 2 hours after food
Do not take with milk, dairy, antacids, calcium, iron or magnesium products - separate them by a few hours
Take with plenty of water and do not lie down immediately afterward to protect your food pipe
Avoid strong sunlight and sunbeds and use sun protection (risk of severe sunburn)
Complete the full course; report severe or bloody diarrhea, severe headache with vision changes, or a blistering rash
Not for use in pregnancy, breastfeeding or children under 8 years; additional contraceptive precautions may be advised
pk: Absorbed within 1-2 hours; bacteriostatic effect during therapy
Peak serum concentration about 2-4 hours after an oral dose
Store at 20-25 C in a tight, light-resistant container; do not use expired tetracyclines
pearls: Classic tetracycline - avoid in pregnancy, breastfeeding and children <8 years (permanent tooth staining, enamel hypoplasia, effects on bone growth)
Cation chelation: dairy, antacids, calcium, iron and magnesium markedly reduce absorption - take on an empty stomach and separate these products
Do NOT use degraded/expired tetracyclines - degradation products can cause a Fanconi-like renal tubular syndrome

Oxytetracycline is an older, USP/FDA-recognized tetracycline; current US systemic monographs are limited, so dosing here reflects established tetracycline-class labeling - doxycycline is often preferred today
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose. Do not double up. Keep taking the medicine until the prescribed course is finished, even if you feel better.
overdose: In overdose, discontinue the drug and treat symptomatically with supportive measures; there is no specific antidote. GI symptoms predominate. Dialysis does not alter the serum half-life and is not beneficial. Hepatic and renal toxicity may occur with very high doses - monitor accordingly.
